The timeout is a positive number of milliseconds (default 30000) and supports parameter expressions. An already matching condition completes immediately. Timeout produces a failed sample and follows the thread group's error policy. Its response message includes the match mode, conditions, resolved operand values, and results from the final evaluation. Individual values longer than 512 characters are abbreviated. Invalid literal numeric operands or regular expressions fail immediately with a 400 response. Unset, empty, or invalid values from parameters or functions count as not matched yet, without logging errors, so another branch can supply a valid value. If they never become valid and match, the action times out normally. Stopping the action interrupts the wait.

New actions default to Ignore on success, so successful waits do not contribute reported samples while failures remain visible. The Results options below the timeout select Included, Ignore on success, or Ignore always. These options change the same sampler result setting as the title menu. Existing saved actions retain their result setting.

The action registers a temporary subscription before checking its conditions and sleeps without periodic polling. Plain parameter expressions subscribe only to their referenced keys, including parameters on the right-hand side. Compiled operands are reused during the wait. Function-based or custom expressions have unknown dependencies and conservatively wake on any parameter write in the same virtual user. Use side-effect-free expressions: functions that write parameters can themselves trigger further evaluations. Subscriptions are removed when the action succeeds, times out, fails, or is interrupted. Fork and parallel parameter views forward subscriptions to the shared store. Conditions must remain true long enough to be observed. Global properties, external state, and objects mutated in place do not trigger notifications; write with vars.put or vars.putObject. Independent virtual users do not share notifications. Start the producer in an asynchronous Fork before reaching the wait.

section.name: Script readiness
section.p: Use Tools > Check script readiness… to check whether the thread groups of a test plan are ready for a performance test. The wizard has four steps: choose the scope (the selected thread groups or all of them), the checks and the validation settings of this run (right-click a thread group and choose Check readiness…, or the Thread Groups section and choose Check readiness of all…, to open the wizard with that scope); run the checks with progress and Cancel; review the findings grouped by check or by transaction; and read the readiness summary. Double-click a finding, or press Enter, to select its element in the tree. Close the wizard to edit the plan; reopening it during the GUI session shows the latest report, and Re-run checks runs them again. Distributed execution, reporting and load generator capacity are out of scope. No external service or AI is used.

Checks marked ⏱ need evidence from a readiness validation. That validation is an ordinary GUI validation of the scope, run with the settings chosen in the wizard for this run only (iterations, timers, time limit); the testplan_validation.* properties keep defining ordinary validation. Without a current readiness validation, these checks are shown as Not verified — requires runtime validation, never hidden.

tr.td: Blocker; Warning when only static resources or redirects are verified
Unresolved variables sent in requests (configuration, confirmed ⏱)
Blocker; Not verified when not configured
Warning when a script reads the previous response body while requests discard bodies; otherwise Suggestion (never affects readiness)

ul.li: Successful validation: the run must complete without request errors or assertion failures. A cancelled, stopped (on error or by a Flow Control Action), timed-out or empty run is never successful. A readiness validation continued with Resume validation counts as complete only when the resumed runs carried every stopped thread group to its end against the same, unchanged plan. Replay from here results are never readiness evidence. The report shows the settings, scope, start and end time and completion status of the run.

Transaction verification coverage: every enabled Transaction Controller with a request sampler needs an enabled assertion, or a Regular Expression, XPath, XPath2, Boundary, CSS Selector, JSON or JMESPath extractor with Fail on no match, applying to one of its samplers under JMeter's scoping rules. Requests outside any transaction are checked one by one. An inner transaction's verification covers the outer one only through its own samplers. Debug Samplers and Flow Control Actions are not requests. After a readiness validation, the check also confirms that a verifying element ran on a covered sampler.

Unused extractions: variables nothing in scope reads, searched in every string field (requests, headers, bodies, controller conditions, assertions, timers, other extractors, configuration), including generated families such as name_1, name_matchNr, name_g1, name_ALL and ForEach inputs, and literal vars.get("name") in scripts. Computed names and scripts reading computed names are reported as possibly used, not unused. An extraction overwritten before any read is reported when both extractions run once in a linear flow.

Unmatched extractions: every invocation of a supported extractor reports whether it matched, whatever Fail on no match says; the resulting variable is never inspected, because it may hold a default or a stale value. Findings show the extractor, source sampler, thread, iteration, expression and a redacted response excerpt. An extractor that never executed is Not verified; other post-processors are Unsupported — not verified.

Extraction processing time: each supported extractor is timed with System.nanoTime(), separately from the request. The response is decoded once before timing starts, so no extractor absorbs a decoding cost shared by all of them. The first invocation is warm-up and reported apart. To get enough observations without replaying requests, each extractor is also run offline against a response captured during validation (20 times by default), with scratch variables. Median, p95 (from 20 observations), maximum and the number of invocations above the budget (3 ms by default) are shown; a median or p95 above the budget is a Warning, and fewer than 5 observations is Not verified.

Think-time review: lists the configured delays between user-facing steps (top-level transactions, or requests outside transactions): timers in effective scope, Flow Control Action pauses and transaction delays. Missing delays, timers that apply to every request of a step (embedded resources included) and several timers on one request are reported for review. Iteration and transaction pacing are listed apart; they are not think time between steps. The check inspects the configuration even when validation ignores timers and never claims a duration is realistic.

Unresolved variables: ${name} references in requests and the request configuration applying to them (HTTP Request Defaults, headers, cookies, authorization) that no variable source in scope defines (User Defined Variables, Test Plan variables, profiles, CSV and structured data sets, extractors, User Parameters, counters, random variables, ForEach). Functions are recognized; properties read with __P are not variables; empty variables are defined. References defined only by scripts, functions or unknown elements, and computed names, are uncertain and resolved by the validation run. During validation, literal ${name} and %24%7Bname%7D in the URL, request headers and request data of what was sent are Blockers, with the cause where the evidence supports it: never defined, its extractor ran without matching, or consumed before it is assigned.

Files and configuration: CSV, JSON/XML/YAML data set, upload and script files and JMX archive entries must exist and be readable, resolving relative paths as the run does. A data set without a file, an HTTP request without a server name or HTTP Request Defaults, and a Module Controller without a target are Blockers. File names computed at run time are Not verified.

Validation exercise coverage: transactions and branches (If, Switch, While, Throughput, Fork, Parallel, Random, Interleave, Once Only, ForEach) that never executed, for example 12 of 14 transactions exercised.

Hardcoded recorded values: values a recorded response returned that later requests still send literally, found with the rules and recorded exchanges of Tools > Correlation Rules. Candidates are for review only; the plan is not changed. Without linked recorded responses, the check is Not verified.

Response body storage: each HTTP request's Processing mode is resolved from its own setting, else the nearest HTTP Request Defaults that sets one, else Store response. A script that reads the previous response body (a JSR223 or BeanShell sampler, pre-processor or timer, or a scripting function such as ${__groovy(prev.getResponseDataAsString())} in a field or a controller condition) is a Warning when any HTTP request of its thread group discards successful bodies (Fetch and discard or Store on error only). Which request runs just before the script depends on the flow (If controllers, loops), so every request of the thread group counts, except requests that keep their bodies because assertions or extractors apply to them. Validation always keeps response bodies, so a validation run does not show the problem: only a test run gives the script an empty body. Without such scripts, the check suggests Store on error only to save memory under load: when most requests inherit Store response, one suggestion on the HTTP Request Defaults (or the thread group) says how many requests would discard successful bodies, which ones must keep Store response (embedded resources, a Save Responses to a file listener saving successful responses, a results file saving response data) and which scripts using the previous result to check first; requests explicitly set to Store response whose bodies nothing reads get a suggestion each. Backend Listeners with the built-in InfluxDB, InfluxDB raw or Graphite clients only send metrics and do not need bodies; custom backend clients and other listeners such as a JSR223 Listener are listed for review, without stopping the suggestion. Scripts are recognized in Java and Groovy forms: prev.getResponseDataAsString(), ctx.getPreviousResult(), ctx.previousResult.responseDataAsString. Assertions and post-processors applying to a request are no reason to keep Store response, because the request keeps its bodies while they apply. Fetch and discard saves the same in steady state but also drops error bodies. With a current readiness validation, the suggestion estimates the successful body bytes per iteration that would no longer be kept. The plan is never changed.

Repeatability: when enabled in the first step, a second validation run in a fresh session (a new thread, so fresh cookies and variables) repeats the scope for the chosen number of iterations (at least two), within its own time limit. Any failure, unmatched extraction or unresolved variable in it is a Blocker.

section.p: Each check is Passed, Blocker, Warning, Review required, Not verified, Not applicable, Accepted or Suggestion, after its worst open finding. Suggestions are optional improvements: a check with only suggestions counts as passed, and they never change the verdict. The summary never gives a score; it shows counts such as 6 of 8 checks passed · 1 blocker · 1 review pending.

ul.li: Ready: every check ran, every mandatory check ran against the current plan and is Passed, Not applicable or Accepted, and no finding is open.
Needs attention: a Blocker, or a Warning or Review finding not covered by an accepted exception.

Not verified: otherwise, for instance when a mandatory check did not run, is Not verified or is based on stale evidence, or when only some checks were selected. Running a subset of the checks never gives Ready.

section.p: Runtime evidence belongs to the plan as it was when the readiness validation started: a fingerprint of the enabled elements in scope, their properties, the validation settings and the scope. Pending editor changes are committed first, and the run uses the usual validation copy of the plan, so editing during a run is safe. When the recomputed fingerprint differs, for example after a field edit, the report marks the evidence Stale and the runtime checks count as Not verified until the next readiness validation. Another validation run, or clearing or opening a plan, also discards it. While a readiness validation runs, other test and validation starts are refused.

Select a finding and use Accept… to record why it is acceptable; Mark… marks an extractor as optional (its failed matches become Warnings) or a transaction or subtree as background/API activity without think time. Exceptions are stored on the element as breaktest.readiness.exception.<check>.<key> properties with the reason, an optional author and the date, so they travel with the script. They do not affect execution or the fingerprint. Recording or removing one is an ordinary plan edit: it can be undone and marks the plan as changed. Accepted findings are shown as Accepted with their reason, never as passes. Exceptions that no longer match a finding are listed as Unused exception. The wizard never adds or weakens assertions and never deletes extractors.

Evidence is kept in memory for the GUI session only, is never written to the JMX and is not logged at INFO or above. Values of Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie headers, and of parameters and JSON keys whose name contains pass, pwd, secret, token, key, auth or session, are masked. Excerpts are limited to about 40 characters around the reference and 512 characters per finding. Set breaktest.readiness.author to choose the default exception author.

ul.li: Large or binary request bodies may be truncated or absent from the request data a sampler records; unresolved values in them are then not verified.
Static analysis follows JMeter's scoping rules but not run-time flow: overwrites are only detected in linear flows, and the consumed-before-assignment cause only for extractors and processors.
Exceptions are kept by editors that preserve unknown properties. A few legacy editors that rebuild their element (FTP, UDP, mail and LDAP samplers and LDAP configuration) can drop them when edited.
Resume validation of a readiness run needs one thread and one iteration, as Resume validation does.
Readiness evidence is not exported; there is no command-line interface in this version.
